case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Statewide Guardian ad Litem Office v. C.C.
key_cases.holding: An appellate court may not reweigh the evidence supporting a termination judgment; because competent substantial evidence supported the trial court's least-restrictive-means and manifest-best-interests findings after the father failed a voluntary case plan, the district court's reversal was quashed.
key_cases.relevance: C.C. treats an accepted and funded voluntary case plan as a genuine rehabilitative effort by the Department.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that the Fifth District's decision improperly reweighed the evidence below and, thus, conflicts with our precedent.

key_cases.case_name: Padgett v. Department of Health & Rehabilitative Services
key_cases.holding: Parental rights may be involuntarily terminated only on clear and convincing proof that reunification poses a substantial risk of significant harm to the child and that termination is the least restrictive means of protecting the child, which ordinarily requires a good-faith agency effort to rehabilitate the parent and reunite the family; abuse of one child may supply grounds as to another child.
key_cases.relevance: Padgett treats a performance agreement or comparable voluntary plan as the ordinary proof that the agency tried rehabilitation before seeking severance.
key_cases.quote: the state must show by clear and convincing evidence that reunification with the parent poses a substantial risk of significant harm to the child

key_cases.case_name: Florida Department of Children & Families v. F.L.
key_cases.holding: Section 39.806(1)(i), which lets the Department petition for termination on the basis of a prior involuntary termination as to a sibling without first offering a case plan for the current child, is constitutional only if construed to require the State to prove — with no rebuttable presumption shifting the burden to the parent — a prior involuntary termination, a substantial risk of significant harm to the current child, and that termination is the least restrictive means of protecting that child.
key_cases.relevance: It establishes that no voluntary service plan need precede a petition grounded on a prior involuntary termination, which limits any argument that an offered voluntary plan is a universal prerequisite.
key_cases.quote: Further, the state must prove that the termination of parental rights is the least restrictive means of protecting the current child from harm.
